Lately, just the sight of storm clouds rolling in sends this wave of panic through me. My chest tightens, I can’t breathe, my heart races like I’m about to collapse. It doesn’t make sense—I’ve never been scared of thunderstorms before. But now, if I’m outside and the sky darkens, I have to get indoors immediately, even if it’s just a passing shower.  

Eating’s been… off, too. I don’t know why, but the thought of swallowing certain foods—especially anything thick or sticky—makes me feel like I’m going to choke. I’ve started cutting back, not because I want to lose weight or anything, but because I can’t shake the fear. It’s not about calories or shape; it’s like my body just revolts at the idea. I skip meals sometimes without noticing. I’m under so much stress I barely register hunger anymore.  

I can’t tell if this is all because I’m burning out or if something deeper’s wrong. The business is tanking, I’m alone most days, and I feel like I’m losing control—but over what, I can’t say.
D012-D021_h001.question_a:

They happen when I’m near anything unpredictable in nature. Like last week, I couldn’t bring myself to walk across a glass skybridge at a rooftop event—my heart exploded in my chest, I broke into a sweat, felt like I was going to pass out. Heights. Just the thought of them now makes my body scream. Same thing during thunderstorms. I’ll be in my apartment, lights off, just trying to power through a work call, and the second thunder cracks, I’m frozen, can’t breathe, have to crawl into a closet until it passes.

I’ve also started avoiding certain foods—specifically ones I think might make me choke, like dry bread or pills. I know it sounds unrelated, but the fear is the same flavor: immediate, irrational, overwhelming. It’s not about my weight or body image—I’ve actually lost weight unintentionally because I’m eating less, but that’s not the point. I avoid food situations purely because I’m terrified of choking, the same way I avoid balconies because I’m terrified of falling. It’s the fear itself that drives the avoidance, not control or shape. This has been going on for years, but with the stress now, it’s worse.
D012-D021_h001.question_b:

I can’t sleep, my chest tightens at the thought of investors pulling out, and honestly, I just don’t feel like eating. I avoid meals with coworkers. Even looking at food—especially carbs or fats—makes me anxious. It’s not that I’m scared of choking or getting sick, like some people might be. It’s that every bite feels like I’m betraying my goals. Gaining weight feels like failure—like losing control, like going soft when everything else is falling apart. I run every morning, no matter how tired I am. If I skip it, I panic—like I’ve already started to let myself go.  

Yeah, I get scared during thunderstorms, and I hate heights—my heart races the second I’m on a high floor. But that’s different. That fear doesn’t drive me to skip dinner. This… this is about staying sharp, lean, in control. Food is the enemy because it makes me fat. And I can’t afford to be fat—not now, not ever.
